3136.body:
## Changes

Accelerate Ming3 0.5B non-streaming synthesis with concurrent cached reference preprocessing, prefill graphs, asynchronous acoustic decode, fused flow arithmetic and exact-length vocoder graphs. Preserve rollback state per launched decode, oversized-batch fallback and non-CUDA vocoder execution.

- Keep captured sampling scales alive. This fixes a correctness bug in main: replay otherwise reads allocator-reusable guidance/noise storage. Raw-main quality and length differences mix this fix with optimization effects; the separate main-plus-lifetime-fix comparison below will isolate that confounder.
- Preserve explicit chunking and graph-disable overrides. Keep unqualified Tiny checkpoints on their previous scheduling, preprocessing placement and vocoder defaults. Support local checkpoint paths containing `@`.
- Share vocoder input/output storage across graph lengths and capture longest first; load only the needed AudioVAE half onto the GPU. Add an explicit fused-flow switch and selected-path logging.
- Bound both reference caches by bytes, support cache bypass, and limit reference duration before GPU encoding. Reject engine-only live weight reloads: restart the whole pipeline to refresh preprocessing replicas, caches and captured constants together.
- Keep current main's Qwen3-Omni graph-lifetime fix from #3152; that file is removed from this PR. Preserve large PCI domains when querying CPU locality through sysfs.

**Changed defaults**

The accelerated defaults apply to the dense 0.5B checkpoint. Tiny retains CPU preprocessing, one preprocessing worker, synchronous decode, no mixed/chunked prefill, no fused flow head, no vocoder graph capture, and `mps: off`.

- Dense preprocessing: CPU → GPU 0; workers 1 → 4. Reference caching uses 256 entries and a 64 MiB budget per cache; `reference_cache_entries: 0` bypasses both caches. Dense references default to a configurable 120-second limit; Tiny retains no duration limit unless explicitly configured.
- Dense decode: async disabled → enabled; chunked prefill disabled → 4096-token chunks; mixed chunks disabled → enabled. Explicit engine overrides win. Prefill graph token counts are 64, 96, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 288, 320, 384, 448 and 512, at most 32 requests. Either graph-disable flag suppresses these stage defaults.
- Dense fused flow arithmetic defaults on; `enable_fused_flow_head: false` selects the module path. Vocoder graphs cover latent lengths 1–384; other lengths run eagerly and `graph_latent_steps: 0` disables capture.
- Dense MPS: off → auto. An inherited `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` is rejected for auto/on; deployments with their own daemon must set `mps: off`. After a hard kill, a stale owner lease may require operator cleanup. Once a GPU is selected, daemon start/verification errors abort startup instead of silently falling back. Short MPS state paths avoid UNIX socket path overflow.

Fragment for an existing dense configuration to disable the accelerated defaults:

```yaml
mps: "off"
stages:
  preprocessing:
    factory:
      max_concurrency: 1
      reference_cache_entries: 0
  tts_engine:
    factory:
      enable_async_decode: false
      enable_fused_flow_head: false
      enable_acoustic_graph: false
      prefill_graph_token_counts: []
    engine:
      chunked_prefill_size: -1
      enable_mixed_chunk: false
      disable_cuda_graph: true
      disable_prefill_cuda_graph: true
  vocoder:
    factory:
      graph_latent_steps: 0
```

## Paired comparison on current main

**Measurement complete; final integration and review pending.** Frozen candidate `3f8593f4cae19fe1c71e929a854bdc03b2c185e6` integrates clean main `0fe60cf6c102caf982430e1764243c6e5c749d76`. Subsequent main changes through `6087f786b3a9dd2d53dee5f321737cecda88dd12` were audited. Qwen3-Omni and streaming-cascade changes do not alter Ming3 synthesis. The ASR audio-loader wrapper was checked on eight real outputs in the pinned image: the available-TorchCodec path produces identical tensors and PCM16 bytes, without creating a CUDA context. The unavailable-decoder fallback is not used in these measurements. The later FlashInfer change selects the same `sm_90a` target on this H200. Later changes affect config discovery and other-model paths. The benchmark server uses an explicit config file, while preparation still resolves model-path defaults; equivalence of later-main preparation is not claimed. New model-registration imports may add startup overhead, which is not measured in these frozen-source cost rows. Final-main integration remains required. The earlier H100 tables and their actual commits are archived in the evidence, not relabeled as current measurements.

Current protocol: one dedicated H200, PyTorch 2.14.1, SGLang 0.5.22, Transformers 5.19.0 and FlashInfer 0.7.1. Model revision `8d66b70a00f05ad183fa8a863b4ce609fc83cbc0`; SeedTTS Arrow `27f4c1adee83b5b29b7c4b375f6b976324bda308`, complete EN 1,088 / ZH 2,020 samples per arm. Each arm has its own saved YAML, resolved native defaults, fresh service and private compilation/reference caches. Common overrides: 64 running requests, graph batch 64 and 2048 client output tokens; warmup equals client concurrency. No CPU quota or affinity override. Per split/concurrency: main seed42 → PR seed42 → PR seed43 → main seed43. All planned ABBA cells and review ablations are complete and independently audited below.

The 92-arm plan covers clean main and a main-plus-sampling-storage-lifetime-fix control at c1/16/32/64 in both languages. Review ablations cover MPS auto/off at EN/ZH c1/c32, reference cache on/off at EN/ZH c32 and fused flow on/off at EN c32. Caching benefits repeated references; it does not establish the same gain for unique-reference traffic. WER and per-sample CAM++ SIM cover all requests. Each arm records WAV hashes, output lengths, failures, startup, one-second sampled device memory and successful graph captures. The same external observer counts successful captures and drains service ports; its logging is included in startup costs.

Means use arithmetic matched-seed averages; p95 is the range of seed percentiles. For each concurrency the overview will use `100 × (sqrt((PR_EN/main_EN) × (PR_ZH/main_ZH)) − 1)`. Adverse quality changes and output-length differences will remain visible.

3189.body:
## Changes

Enable opt-in streaming audio for Ming3 Tiny. Dependency order is **#3136 → #3189 → #3190**. The two feature PRs must land together after the prerequisite; do not merge either into its temporary dependency branch. Retarget each to `main` after its prerequisite merges and recheck integration/CI.

- Extract the existing Ming-Omni-TTS batched AudioVAE decoder and streaming scheduler into `sglang_omni/modules/ming_audio/`; both model adapters reuse it. Keep the old Ming-TTS imports compatible.
- Batch active requests into fixed incremental cache slots, with cancellation and late-chunk cleanup. Preserve terminal `finish_reason`, usage and the final tail.
- Preserve #3136's full vocoder CUDA-graph path for `stream=false`; `stream=true` uses incremental attention/interpolation/ISTFT state. CPU non-streaming keeps its full decoder fallback.
- Update the explicitly requested Ming3 cookbook's `stream=true` behavior and deployment defaults.

**Changed defaults**

Streaming remains opt-in (`stream=true`, `response_format=pcm`). The default chunk is eight latent steps, with a fixed cache capacity of 32. The first non-empty packet needs latent 17; shorter utterances flush at completion. Eight steps is a decoder grouping parameter, not an elapsed-time latency promise. Non-streaming deployment and graph defaults come from #3136.

## Paired comparison on current main

This is a feature PR: main has no incremental Ming3 endpoint, so no independent main-to-PR throughput gain is claimed. The following compares streaming and non-streaming modes of the integrated implementation, not a clean-main performance baseline. Full-corpus WER/SIM were not measured in this latency run.

Tiny latency measurement source: `251f02b467fe06269cb2d3d8c1063565d7c3de82`, tree `3e68505e3a2c26ae6e88e8360007bc0d3896d5d7`, measured October 27, 2026. Current head `c864715c205d995835b48e26ca1d10cffff9350c` retains dense enablement in the companion PR. Integration with main `0fe60cf6` was checked on `14f5355e`/`348f6973`; the subsequent one-line capability declaration correction affects startup logging only. Synthesis, scheduling and tensor paths are unchanged.

Tiny uses one preprocessing worker and does not enter the bounded worker-pool path changed in main; its latency table retains the actual original source above. Both checkpoints passed fresh HTTP and paired-ASR checks on `348f6973`. Dense GPU preprocessing was remeasured separately in all 16 mode blocks and is reported in #3190. Later main `39fbbbf` only adds Qwen3-Omni token-budget handling/tests and an unused-by-Ming3 constant.

Protocol: one dedicated H200; PyTorch 2.14.1, SGLang 0.5.22, Transformers 5.19.0. Tiny model revision `7bd9446a8d47e462362261a0150258da6d458318`; dense revision `8d66b70a00f05ad183fa8a863b4ce609fc83cbc0`. SeedTTS Arrow `27f4c1adee83b5b29b7c4b375f6b976324bda308`, first 128 EN and 128 ZH samples, all with reference audio/text conditioning. Per split/concurrency: nonstream seed42 → stream seed42 → stream seed43 → nonstream seed43. Native benchmark, warmup equal to concurrency, automatic pipeline config, default max-running/graph-batch 32. Dense uses native MPS auto; Tiny uses MPS off. One service per model spans all 16 blocks, so compilation and speaker caches persist; each block still runs its native warmup. Dense prompt-latent caching is seed-keyed: stream42 can reuse nonstream42, while stream43 first introduces seed43. Tiny still encodes reference prompts in its engine. Results describe this replay/cache protocol, not cold-reference latency or a cache-normalized A/B estimate. No CPU quota or affinity override. Means are arithmetic seed means; p95s are the two seed values' range, never averaged. Each completed row contains 256 attempts.

Enable opt-in streaming audio for Ming3 dense 0.5B. Dependency order is **#3136 → #3189 → #3190**. Retarget each to `main` after its prerequisite merges and recheck integration/CI.

- Enable dense 0.5B streaming on the shared batched AudioVAE backend introduced in #3189.
- Emit generated latents only, excluding reference-conditioning latents, and test the five-step minimum terminal flush.
- Preserve #3136's CUDA graph path for `stream=false`; use incremental cache state for `stream=true`, including accurate finish reason and usage.

**Changed defaults**

Streaming remains opt-in (`stream=true`, `response_format=pcm`). The default chunk is eight latent steps, with a fixed cache capacity of 32. The first non-empty packet needs latent 17; shorter utterances flush at completion. Eight steps is a decoder grouping parameter, not an elapsed-time latency promise. Non-streaming deployment and graph defaults come from #3136.

## Paired comparison on current main

This is a feature PR: main has no incremental Ming3 endpoint, so no independent main-to-PR throughput gain is claimed. The following compares streaming and non-streaming modes of the integrated implementation, not a clean-main performance baseline. Full-corpus WER/SIM were not measured in this latency run.

Measurement source for all tables below: `348f6973d4878ed77a9c6c60d072c91addaf15d8`, integrating main `0fe60cf6c102caf982430e1764243c6e5c749d76`, measured October 27, 2026 UTC. Current head `0ef18ce8952e027650d82d4292785e9687dface8` differs from this measurement source only in the static streaming capability declaration used by startup logging and the cookbook clarification; synthesis, scheduling and tensor paths are unchanged. All 16 dense mode blocks completed: 2,048 successful requests, including 1,024 streaming requests. The original `251f02b4` measurements remain dated historical evidence. Previously audited main `39fbbbfed68715710917130654b115d3d514b768` only adds Qwen3-Omni token-budget handling and an unused-by-Ming3 request-data constant; it does not change this measured path.

Protocol: one dedicated H200; PyTorch 2.14.1, SGLang 0.5.22, Transformers 5.19.0. Per split/concurrency: nonstream seed42 → stream seed42 → stream seed43 → nonstream seed43. Native benchmark, warmup equal to concurrency, automatic pipeline config, default max-running/graph-batch 32. Dense uses native MPS auto; Tiny uses MPS off. One service per model spans all 16 blocks, so compilation and speaker caches persist; each block still runs its native warmup. Dense prompt-latent caching is seed-keyed: stream42 can reuse nonstream42, while stream43 first introduces seed43. Tiny still encodes reference prompts in its engine. Results describe this replay/cache protocol, not cold-reference latency or a cache-normalized A/B estimate. No CPU quota or affinity override. 3217.body:
## Changes

**Draft dependency stack: #3136 → #3189 → #3190 → #3217.** This PR contains the Tiny precision and graph increment over the two separate streaming PRs. This is the top layer of native [stack #3254](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/stack/3254), with #3190 as its temporary base. The two streaming PRs remain separate. After the prerequisites land, verify the rebased main integration. Do not merge it into a dependency branch.

- Preserve Tiny native-precision acoustic computation inside CUDA graphs, with owned timestep/rotary/projection storage and native-rounding normalization; preserve eager and gradient paths.
- Reuse request noise storage without advancing its random generator, and warm both Triton KDA prefill branches using private state before readiness.
- For `stream=false`, retain Tiny's complete exact-length AudioVAE graphs, clone replay outputs, and fall back eagerly outside captured lengths. Dense keeps #3136's decoder-transformer graph path.
- For `stream=true`, retain the shared incremental AudioVAE cache path from #3189/#3190. A CUDA regression checks both Tiny and dense dispatch and verifies that streaming never invokes the non-streaming graph decoder.

**Changed defaults**

- Tiny uses GPU preprocessing with four workers, asynchronous decode, prefill graph buckets and `mps: auto`, versus the prerequisite's conservative Tiny defaults. These acoustic/preprocessing settings affect both request modes.
- Tiny CUDA/Triton KDA prefill compilation moves to startup warmup; there is no separate KDA-warmup opt-out.
- Tiny CUDA vocoding captures through `min(graph_latent_steps, maximum_decode_steps)` (250 for this checkpoint); the configured graph limit remains 384. Set `stages.vocoder.factory.graph_latent_steps: 0` to disable vocoder capture. Capture happens at startup even when subsequent requests stream.
- Reference caching retains its 64 MiB cap, and Tiny has no default reference-duration cap. Streaming remains opt-in with PCM output, using the prerequisite's incremental cache.

## Paired comparison on current main

**Current independent performance qualification is pending.** Head `8d0f5d4352b704986cbc50e44ec4df42cce0fbc9` integrates the streaming head `0ef18ce8` and #3136 `3f8593f4`. Compare this increment with actual main after those prerequisites land. The historical 32-arm bundle used different source revisions and CPU settings and included #3136; it is not an independent gain for this head. The earlier #3189 Tiny latency measurements are also not measurements of these changed Tiny defaults.

Required protocol: pinned Tiny revision `7bd9446a8d47e462362261a0150258da6d458318`; full SeedTTS `27f4c1adee83b5b29b7c4b375f6b976324bda308`, EN 1,088 / ZH 2,020 requests; both modes at c1/16/32/64; seeds42/43 in A42/B42/B43/A43 order; fresh services/private caches and native configurations with matching benchmark overrides. Retain all-request WER, CAM++ SIM, output lengths, failures and startup/memory/graph costs. Report arithmetic seed means, p95 ranges and geometric EN/ZH throughput changes only from complete paired cells; streaming also needs first-audio and underrun measurements.

### Non-streaming

| Concurrency | EN/ZH geometric throughput change |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Pending |
| 16 | Pending |
| 32 | Pending |
| 64 | Pending |

Independent req/s, response latency, WER, SIM and failure tables are pending. First packet is N/A for completed non-streaming responses.

### Streaming

| Concurrency | EN/ZH geometric throughput change |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Pending |
| 16 | Pending |
| 32 | Pending |
| 64 | Pending |

The incremental vocoder path is retained, but Tiny acoustic/preprocessing changes can affect its latency and quality. Independent req/s, response latency, first-audio, underrun, WER, SIM and failure tables are pending; functional parity does not establish performance parity.

## Costs

| Metric | Main after prerequisites | This increment | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Startup to ready | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Peak sampled TTS device memory | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Successful graph captures | Pending | Pending | Pending |

The increment adds KDA warmup, complete exact-length vocoder graphs and concurrent GPU preprocessing. The functional smoke confirmed 250 complete Tiny vocoder captures, but it is not an independent cost comparison. Historical bundle costs remain archived.

## Tests

<!-- current-main-cpu-integration -->
Additional cumulative integration check: `8d0f5d4` merged locally with main `e9c0584` (tree `4c02de0`, unpublished) is conflict-free. CPU Torch 2.14.1 tests: **606 passed, 42 skipped, 2 failed**. Both failures are unchanged shared stream-priority tests whose monkeypatch setup requires `torch.cuda.Stream.priority_range`, absent in the CPU wheel; all collected Ming-family tests passed. No tests were deselected or relaxed. This does not replace current-head CUDA CI or final merged-series validation. [Full integration evidence](https://github.com/Zhuofeng-Li/sglang-omni/blob/codex/ming3-streaming-review-evidence/evidence/ming3-current-main-integration/report.md).
<!-- current-main-cpu-integration-end -->

- Exact head `8d0f5d4`: **428 H100 tests passed, 6 skipped**, covering Ming3/Ming-TTS, native arithmetic, graph/eager behavior, both Tiny/dense graph-versus-cache dispatch cases, MPS, CPU locality, shared scheduler and stage environment. The six skips are unsupported strided-normalization tiles with eager fallback. Full pre-commit passed; CodeQL protocol stubs explicitly raise `NotImplementedError`.
- Real Tiny weights: **14 PCM cases passed**, plus SSE terminal metadata, concurrent streams, disconnect recovery and a one-latent terminal flush. All four EN/ZH × reference/no-reference full/stream pairs had matching sample counts and normalized ASR transcripts. These are small functional checks, not full-corpus quality qualification.
- Smoke profile: one H100 80GB, PyTorch 2.14.1 / SGLang 0.5.22 / Transformers 5.19.0, `mem-fraction-static=0.6` and max-running/graph-batch 32. All 65 downloaded model files matched the pinned Hub revision and Git/LFS hashes. GPU clients, containers and test ports were cleaned up; the assignment was released after verified off-node backup.
- [Exact-head manual Omni CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/actions/runs/40466048020): all unit partitions **passed** on `8d0f5d4` — CPU A **4,733 passed / 87 skipped**, CPU B **5,308 / 36**, accelerator **1,145 / 34**. Both Tiny/dense graph-versus-cache routing cases passed. The full manual workflow and environment cleanup completed successfully. Preflight verified the exact head, `run_unit_test=true`, all model stages false and no model preset (`run-unit-test-ci-only`). The automatic workflow’s draft gate is expected; it is not a passing GPU check.
- The latest CI guide, resolver, workflows and live labels were checked at main `335d32b0`. No PR stage label is added while draft. Other models do not substitute for target validation.
- The only changed documentation path is the explicitly requested `docs/cookbook/ming3_tts.md`. Dependency landing, final-main integration, independent performance/quality/cost qualification and approval remain pending.

Developed using [RSI-Harness](https://github.com/OpenRSI-Foundation/OpenRSI-Index/tree/main/RSI-Harness) in [OpenRSI-Index](https://github.com/OpenRSI-Foundation/OpenRSI-Index); [validation, source records and historical evidence](https://github.com/Zhuofeng-Li/sglang-omni/blob/codex/ming3-streaming-review-evidence/evidence/ming3-tiny-stream-integration/report.md).
